findings.title: Pinned 20-entry review manifest names an untracked gitignored file
findings.evidence: `.logs/d110c-0c1b-plan-review-d4ed7024/manifest.sha256:8` lists `./grok/stderr.log` (empty-file digest `e3b0c442…`), but `git ls-files --error-unmatch` reports that path is unknown to git and it is absent from commit `56cdba29`'s 20 changed files under that directory; `.gitignore:14` is `*.log`. The manifest's own SHA-256 recomputes to `7c3592e1edb59992740be65d7565cf3105f80c0e9b188ec51f2f160fa227e88c`, matching plan line 96336 exactly, and the audit manifest/audit.md hashes (`08d27843…`, `1227676a…`) also verify.
findings.impact: A verifier who checks out tree `ebe75e12…` and runs `sha256sum -c manifest.sha256` gets a missing-file failure on entry 8, so the plan's "validating 20-entry self-excluding manifest" claim does not verify from the pushed tree alone. No evidence content is lost (the file is zero bytes), and this is the same convention as the already-approved predecessor `.logs/d110c-0c1a-review-confirmation-7414fa6b/manifest.sha256:12`.
findings.required_action: Owner: the D.110c-0c1b custody/plan owner. Disposition: accept as the repo's pre-existing `*.log` custody convention and change nothing in this slice, or (if a from-tree-only replay is wanted later) `git add -f` the empty log and re-pin the manifest hash. Not a RED blocker; no recursive review.

findings.title: "another close bind still refuse" is imprecise for an already-bound plane
findings.evidence: Plan lines 96297–96298 say "another local issue and another close bind still refuse until deactivation/recovery." For the pre-bound ordering the plane is already in the `bindings` WeakMap, so `bindCreatorLiveClose` returns at `packages/node/src/creator-close.ts:549-550` with the cached handle and `ok: true` — it never reaches `claimCreatorCloseRegistration` (:551) or `CREATOR_CLOSE_UNAVAILABLE` (:552). The refusal instead surfaces on the retried `close()`, which is permitted because the outer catch resets `closeTask = undefined` (:805) and re-aborts the stage (:806), so the retry re-enters `stageSnapshot()` → fold recheck → `creator snapshot export failed: not-active` (:608-611).
findings.impact: A GREEN test author reading only that summary sentence could assert a bind-time `CREATOR_CLOSE_UNAVAILABLE` on the already-bound plane and get `{ ok: true, handle }` instead — the same class of unproducible-token trap the P1 correction removed. The plan's authoritative pins at lines 96283–96285 and 96291–96294 are correct and already distinguish the two orderings, so this is wording, not scope.
findings.required_action: Owner: the D.110c-0c1b RED/GREEN test author. Disposition: for the pre-bound ordering assert the repeat refusal on the retried `close()` (existing `creator snapshot export failed: not-active`), and reserve the `CREATOR_CLOSE_UNAVAILABLE` assertion for a plane with no prior binding. No plan-text edit or executable-scope change required before RED.

summary: All six corrections are confirmed against source, and the corrected tests-only RED is causal with the frozen GREEN closing it in scope. (1) The token demotion is forced by the code: `snapshotExportFailure(\"not-active\", staged.detail)` (v3-live.ts:7029) discards the fold detail and creator-close.ts:611 throws ``creator snapshot export failed: ${snapshot.kind}``, while a refused mint returns undefined → `CREATOR_CLOSE_UNAVAILABLE` (creator-close.ts:552); neither surface can carry a new product token under the no-new-API freeze. (2) The `ISSUANCE_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN` arm is real in both stores — node COMMITs at node-issuance-store.ts:802 then reaches `#classifyAfterTerminalSuppression` (:819), whose unreadable readback throws `UnknownOutcomeFailure` (terminal.ts:126, contract.ts:45); browser is identical at :748-766 — and at v3-live.ts:5682-5687 a no-policy plane (`reservation === undefined`, `signerResolved === true`) sets no halt today, which is exactly the gap. Halting on that exact code while keeping the `!signerResolved && !terminalTransactionStarted` release discriminator preserves the retained E5-01 gate, whose fixture rejects `transactIssue` with a plain TypeError before signing (e5-01-v3-operation-admission-red.test.ts:186-199); the capacity throw stays pre-transaction inside `buildAndSign` (node-issuance-store.ts:600). (3) The sequence-0 prefix is materially necessary, not cosmetic: with a single omitted row `deriveCreatorIssuanceRetirementBoundary` leaves `admitted === null` and throws `CREATOR_ISSUANCE_RETIREMENT_UNAVAILABLE` (creator-issuance-retirement-boundary.ts:130-132), so the close would refuse for D.110c-0c1a reasons; with seq 0 in-graph it truncates (`truncated = true`, admitted = 0) and advances, and the next-epoch refusal is genuinely caused by `decoded.anchor !== currentAnchorDigest` at :116-122. (4) Both orderings hold — the fold queues behind the in-flight issue via the shared gate (enqueueRegistrationTask:3961, stageBlueprintEpoch:6714, enqueueLocalIssue:5908), creator-close calls `abortSnapshotStage()` on the failed export at :610 and again at :806 (clearing only `blueprintClosing`, v3-live.ts:6991-6996, leaving `operationAdmissionHalted` set), and `claimedCreatorCloseHandles.add` runs only on a successful mint (v3-live.ts:2591) so a refused mint consumes no claim. (5) The halt reuse is accurately described: it is read at v3-live.ts:3727 (ingress) and :5600 (local issue, ahead of any store call, so a second issue truly cannot re-transact), and it is only ever set on failure, so the no-failure hot path is untouched; the retained frontier/batching gates never pair `retryAfterFailure` with `failJournalAtIssuedOrdinal`, so the unconditional `committedFailure()` halt does not break them. (6) Recovery remains the sole reconciliation owner — the outbox scan at v3-live.ts:5031-5199 authenticates and admits the exact row, and the fresh registration with `operationAdmissionHalted: false` (:7290) is built only from a recovered capability (:7263). The diff touches only the plan, the audit, and review evidence; no schema, wire, API, dependency, authority, workload, threshold, or campaign change appears. All three pinned hashes recompute exactly. Two P2s remain, both with named owners and neither blocking RED.
